title: Comprehensive benchmarking of RNA velocity methods across single-cell datasets.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed Zenodo record 18051944 (CC-BY-4.0): 31 zipped processed AnnData (h5ad, a single-cell matrix format) files, 4 MB to 2.84 GB each, plus 00_Processed_AnnData_Summary.xlsx, which I opened. Its Ground_truth column holds 3-5 hand-picked cell-type transition pairs per dataset (e.g. ('Ngn3 high EP','Pre-endocrine')). Also listed Zenodo 20183808 (benchmark code, MIT, 87 MB) and 20183828 (VeloEV evaluation package, MIT, 1.1 MB).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: 19 tools / 30 methods, 34 datasets (26 real, 8 simulated), eight evaluation tasks. I did not open any h5ad file or count cells.

a1_downloadable.note: Zenodo files are open (CC-BY-4.0); I saw the file listing and downloaded the summary xlsx.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No per-cell measured outcome. The benchmark's 'ground truth' is a list of 3-5 expected cluster-to-cluster transitions per dataset (seen in the summary xlsx). Any per-cell target would have to be built from those curated edges or from method outputs.

a3_inputs_present.note: Spliced and unspliced count layers are in the AnnData objects, according to the summary xlsx (files themselves not opened).

a4_units_stated.note: Raw counts, per the summary xlsx.

a5_enough_rows.note: The natural labelled unit is the dataset or transition edge: about 34 datasets x 3-5 edges, so roughly 100-150 labels (estimated from the xlsx, not counted exactly). That is far below the 400 minimum.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: a few small h5ad files (<200 MB each); the largest are 1.0-2.8 GB zipped
a6_fits_laptop.note: Small subsets fit; the full collection is about 10 GB zipped.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not fully checked: the paper says 34 datasets, Zenodo holds 31 h5ad files for 26 real datasets, and simulated data comes from the code record.

a8_label_provenance.note: Velocity vectors are themselves model outputs, and the 'ground truth' transitions are author-chosen biological priors, not measurements. Predicting either one means copying methods or annotations.

backbone.name: scGPT / Geneformer (single-cell foundation models) would be the only candidates

honest_claim_h3: A model could only claim to reproduce the authors' chosen transition directions on about 34 datasets, which is not a learnable prediction task.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a dataset's single-cell gene-count features to predict which RNA velocity method will best recover known cell-state transitions.
plain_idea.train_on: One example per benchmark dataset (about 34; 31 processed files verified on Zenodo), described by summary features of its spliced and unspliced counts.
plain_idea.predict: Which method ranks best, using the benchmark's scores. Those scores compare velocity outputs with 3-5 author-curated cell-type transitions per dataset.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: It would point users to a velocity method without running all 30, but with about 34 examples a lookup table of the paper's own guidance does the same job.

ml_idea: Considered meta-learning: predicting the best RNA velocity method (velocity = inferred direction of change in each cell's gene expression) from dataset features. Rejected because there are only about 34 datasets and the labels are curated priors or model outputs.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; rejected at Part A.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the Ground_truth transition pairs in 00_Processed_AnnData_Summary.xlsx (done: 3-5 per dataset).

verdict_reason: This is a methods benchmark. Its 'ground truth' is 3-5 author-curated cell-type transitions per dataset (verified in the summary xlsx), and velocity values are themselves model outputs. So there is no measured label column (A2, A8), and about 34 datasets is too few to learn from (A5).
